title: bus_client publishes a held connection to a home's bus
intention: bus_client's remote.held_connection(home) opens one connection to the bus at home, dialled at socket_path(home), and holds it until the with block ends: while held the bus counts it open, and on exit, error or not, it is released.
why: Measured 2026-11-20 on akiendelllinux: c234aae2c0b9's PROVED was refused at clearance, deterministic red [sole_path_holds] bus/proofs/test_a_scratch_bus_with_no_caller_ends_itself.py imports ['socket']: its _open_connection_guard (line 256 at ff0c46fe2) dials a raw AF_UNIX socket to <home>/bus.sock to hold a connection open. A proof that needs a connection held has no door to hold one through, so it reaches past the sole path; and the raw dial spells the address by hand where e44cf1f23c84 makes socket_path(home) its one spelling.
traces_to: RULE 1 (a proof reaches the bus only through bus_client, the sole path); Law 4 (sole_path_holds is the physics, and it reds a raw dial).
how: Add held_connection to remote.py beside exchange; a red-first proof in bus_client's proofs holds a scratch bus open past a short CAIRN_BUS_IDLE_S and watches it idle out after release. Rides e44cf1f23c84 for socket_path. c234aae2c0b9's proof edit then uses it.

clauses.claim: while held, the bus counts the connection open: a scratch bus started by ensure_bus(home, scratch=True) with CAIRN_BUS_IDLE_S=3 and held_connection(home) entered stays up past 3 s + slack, with no record in <home>/stops.jsonl
on exit the connection is released: after the with block ends, the same bus exits by idle within 3 s + slack and its stop record's cause is 'idle'
an exception raised inside the with block still releases it: the bus idles out after, as in clause 2, and the exception reaches the caller unchanged
the holder dials socket_path(home): with no bus at home, entering held_connection(home) raises an error whose text names str(socket_path(home)), and nothing is created at that path

decisions.text: D1: remote.py publishes held_connection(home=None, *, timeout=_TIMEOUT_S), a contextlib.contextmanager that connects one AF_UNIX stream socket to socket_path(home) (the e44cf1f23c84 spelling, never <home>/bus.sock by hand), yields it unread and unwritten, and closes it in a finally. A failed connect raises (Law 7) naming the path; it never spawns a bus (ensure_bus is the starter). The name joins remote's public surface (its module docstring's list).

D2: a red-first proof, PROVES {1,2,3,4}, one tooth per clause, imports held_connection inside each tooth (it is what the build adds). Each tooth starts its own bus with ensure_bus(home, scratch=True, env={'CAIRN_BUS_IDLE_S': '3'}) at its own scratch home, reads <home>/stops.jsonl (the home is the proof's own), and stops every unit it started by name (remote._unit) in a finally. It imports no socket.

out: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs (c234aae2c0b9's proof edit is its own)

measured.saw: c234aae2c0b9 PROVED refused at clearance: [sole_path_holds] bus/proofs/test_a_scratch_bus_with_no_caller_ends_itself.py imports ['socket'], from _open_connection_guard's raw AF_UNIX dial to <home>/bus.sock
